text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak says after meeting King Hussein: if the situation in the region continues as it is, the peace process may be totally destroyed. Hussein: the Washington summit did not change the situation... and showed just how wise Mubarak was not to attend it.
- Thirteen bodies removed from the rubble and victims rise to 27. Two girls -- an Egyptian and American -- rescued after 36 hours under the rubble.
- Camlah, the building owner whose apartment block collapsed on top of its residents during the 1992 earthquake, is sentenced to 10 years in jail.
- After three hours of talks in Sharm el-Sheikh, Mubarak and Hussein say efforts continuing to support the peace process.
- The collapse of the Heliopolis building is proof of the corruption in local council, says Editor-in-chief Galal Dewidar in fronted column.
- The committee in charge of investigating the reasons for collapse will have results by next week. Draft law to stiffen punishment for building owners who break construction specifications.
- A morgue worker at Kasr el-Aini hospital steals eyes of the dead!
- Mubarak says the stalemate could destroy the Middle East peace process.
- Parliament to discuss in its next session banning any renovation work inside apartments unless owners obtain official permission.
- Former Sudanese information minister among the dead in Cairo building collapse.
